summary:
As humanity prepares to establish lunar bases and venture farther into space, understanding flame behavior across different gravity environments is essential for managing fire and explosion hazards.

For decades, NASA has accumulated extensive microgravity combustion data. However, their volume makes it difficult to compare combustion behavior on Earth, aboard the ISS, and on the Moon, while data for partial-gravity environments remain limited.

Our service helps researchers select, visualize, and interpret relevant information from tens of terabytes of experimental data. It organizes data from NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository into a hierarchical ontology, accessible through conversations with Ddonguri, our AI data exploration agent. Through continued interaction, the ontology becomes increasingly tailored to each user.

A physics-based flame simulation engine informed by existing data supports hypothesis generation and preliminary testing in environments with limited experimental data, including partial gravity. It also shows how simulation results relate to existing experimental observations.

By connecting data exploration and simulation in one intuitive conversational workflow, the service will accelerate research on fire safety in space and help humanity take its next step in space exploration.
details:
Project Overview

Our project is an AI-assisted environment for exploring combustion science data from NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository. It connects conversational data discovery, interactive visual analysis, and data-driven flame simulation in one workflow, helping researchers move from experimental observations to hypothesis generation and preliminary testing.

How It Works and Key Features

1. Playground: Conversational Data Discovery

Users interact with ddonguri, our AI data exploration agent, to identify, select, and understand data relevant to their research objectives. A hierarchical ontology structures the data and guides discovery. Through continued conversation, the ontology becomes increasingly tailored to each user’s needs.

2. Data Explorer: Interactive Visual Analysis

Users explore original PSI records, experimental conditions, and results through interactive visualizations. This helps them interpret flame behavior, compare observations, and understand how experimental conditions relate to combustion behavior.

3. Laboratory: Data-Driven Flame Simulation

Users work with Donggeuri to adjust virtual environmental conditions and explore differences in flame behavior. A physics-based flame simulation engine informed by NASA experimental data supports hypothesis generation and preliminary testing, including exploration of partial-gravity conditions where experimental data remain limited. Simulation results are presented in relation to existing experimental observations.

4. Bilingual Interface

The interface supports English and Korean, making data exploration and interaction with ddonguri accessible in both languages.

Technology Stack

  • Programming languages: Python, JavaScript
  • Backend: FastAPI
  • Agent–tool integration: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
  • Containerization: Docker
  • Frontend: React, Vite
  • Interactive graphics: WebGL

What Makes the Project Creative?

The project brings an approachable AI guide, a personalized ontology, interactive visualizations, and flame simulation into a connected research environment. Its creative contribution is the continuity between finding relevant evidence, understanding it, and using it to explore new hypotheses. Ddonguri provides a familiar conversational interface across data discovery and simulation.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project aims to:

  • Make large experimental datasets easier to understand and analyze through guided conversation and intuitive visual interaction.
  • Improve research relevance by using an ontology to select and organize data around each user’s objectives.
  • Support exploration of combustion in space environments through flame simulation informed by NASA experimental data, including conditions with limited experimental coverage.

The intended impact is to accelerate research on fire safety in space by connecting experimental evidence, data interpretation, and simulation within an accessible workflow.

Design Considerations

  • Data volume and research relevance: Help researchers focus on the experimental records most relevant to their questions.
  • Experimental context: Present experimental conditions alongside results to support meaningful interpretation and comparison.
  • Limited partial-gravity data: Use simulation to generate and preliminarily test hypotheses where experimental observations are scarce.
  • Usability and personalization: Combine an approachable agent, interactive visualizations, and an ontology that adapts through continued interaction.
  • Language accessibility: Support both English and Korean interfaces.
